newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks close mixed ahead of U.S. payrolls data.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks close mixed ahead of U.S. payrolls data.

text.p: Australian shares closed mixed on Friday with profit-taking waning late in the session but investors still cautious ahead of the release of key September U.S. payrolls data later on Friday.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index ended 0.6 points up at 2,315.5, after touching an intra-day low of 2,306.
The December share price index finished five points down at 2,340 and at a 24.5 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said profit-taking in bank stocks ended late in the session with that sector's recovery helping to lift the market into slightly positive territory.

"The imminent release of U.S. payrolls data kept the market fairly quiet today and what happens in the U.S. tonight should set the tone for the market early next week," said Jim Tredenick, a dealer at Brisbane brokerage, Nevitts.

Tredenick said speculation of a further local interest rate cut was spurred by comments from Treasurer Peter Costello earlier in the day but that generally investors had discounted the likelihood of a rate cut in the near term.
"I don't think the local employment data (to be released next Thursday) even if it is weak, will be enough to rekindle the type of speculation we saw earlier this week," he said.

Dealers said it was apparent Dutch telecom and postal group KPN actively bought TNT stock again today after its takeover bid on Wednesday. KPN is allowed to lift its stake in TNT to a threshold of 19.9 percent.
In other trading, shares of chemical manufacturer ICI Australia slipped following the company's announcement late on Thursday that it knew of no reason for its recent share price rise.
The announcement poured cold water on recent speculation that the company's U.K. parent, ICI Plc, was about to launch a mop-up bid for the company, dealers said.
